sd_sunshine.blurb: Sunshine is a long cliff in Spearfish Canyon, roughly 26 miles up the canyon from the town of Spearfish, split into more than a dozen separately named walls. Spearfish Canyon’s rock is pocketed limestone, and the routes here are bolted. Nearly everything here is sport climbing, with a handful of boulder problems. Most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a fair number of 5.13s too, while easier leads are scarce. The Bunny Slope is the usual place for newer leaders to start, and Thunderhead is steep, bouldery and holds a lot of the hard lines. Other big walls are Big Black Face and Land of the Shorties. The cliff is a favorite on warm winter days, and in summer the shade arrives after about four in the afternoon.

wy_old_road_crags.blurb: The Old Road Crags are a cluster of walls in Ten Sleep Canyon, east of the town of Ten Sleep in the Bighorn Mountains, scattered on both sides of Ten Sleep Falls near the bottom of the old dirt road. The canyon as a whole is known for limestone with pockets, edges and flakes, and the climbing here is almost all sport. Routes mostly run 5.10 to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.11 and 5.12 range and only a thin supply of easy ones. Powers Wall is a pocketed face that runs from vertical to slightly overhanging, with rock quality that varies across it. Honky Tonk, Greenland and the Leigh Creek walls add more variety. The canyon is at its best in midsummer, and its crags offer a mix of sun and shade.

ca_d_camp_4_area.blurb: Camp 4 sits on the north side of Yosemite Valley, close to the foot of the granite walls near Yosemite Falls, and has long been a gathering point for climbers. Most of what is here is bouldering on big, polished granite blocks scattered through the woods, a short stroll from the camp itself, with a smaller set of traditional routes on the cliffs nearby. Problems cover the full range, from easy warm-ups through the middle grades to a good number of hard V-grade lines. The roped routes mostly sit between 5.8 and 5.11. Standouts include the Camp 4 Wall, Lower Brother, Wine Boulder and the Big Columbia Boulder.

ca_lassen_national_park.blurb: Lassen National Park sits in northeast California where the Sierra and the Cascades come together, and its climbing is on volcanic rock. The crags are mostly single-pitch and mix trad, sport, top-rope and bouldering, with a few alpine routes too. Grades stretch from easy fifth class to the low 5.13s, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10 and 5.11. Eagle Peak is the biggest crag, a long band of rock high on the mountain where you can stay out of the heat and still have sun. Raker Peak is a west-facing band that varies from solid rock to crumbly. Most crags need a hike of half an hour or more, and snow can cover the approaches into early summer.

ca_lower_gorge.blurb: The Lower Gorge is the downstream stretch of Owens River Gorge near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. The gorge is cut into volcanic tuff, with climbing on edges, pockets and cracks, and it is known as a very concentrated sport-climbing destination that works through most of the year, though summers can run hot. This section is overwhelmingly bolted, with a small number of trad and top-rope lines. Routes run from easy to the 5.12s, and the strongest showing is in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with plenty of moderates as well. Warning Signs and Blocky Top are the largest walls, with Diamond Face and Pink Face close behind. Pink Face faces northwest, gives early shade and rarely gets busy.

nv_route_158.blurb: Route 158 is the road through the high crags of Mount Charleston, northwest of Las Vegas, running between Kyle and Lee Canyons. Sport climbing dominates, and the grades lean hard: most routes run from 5.11 through 5.14, with only a modest number of easier ones. There is also a strong boulder presence, mostly in the moderate to hard V-grades. Robber's Roost, on limestone, is the largest hub by far, with several named walls and a cave, and it is shady enough to be a refuge on hot days. Other crags include the Glass House, Starter Crag and the Icehouse. It is busy at the Roost almost any day, so solitude is not part of the deal.
